newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly firmer but fuel flat.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly firmer but fuel flat.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly stronger on Wednesday, traders said.
Gas oil was $2 or so firmer, despite premiums coming under pressure, thanks to a $4 a tonne gain on IPE futures.
Premiums lost up to $2 a tonne, weighed down by good supplies, mild weather and lacklustre demand. "Its devastatingly weak and an almost non-existent market," said one trader.
A distressed 25,000 tonne Libyan cargo was sold at high cif 0.2 quotes -$1.50 cif Southern France. Russian premiums were heard as low as high cif 0.2 quotes -50 cents cif Med against Tuesday's +$2.
Naphtha rose $5 to $220/$222 cif due to the sharp jump in crude futures and some end-user demand. Traders said buyers were trying to overcome high freight rates by combining cargoes.

Shipping sources said Mira fixed the 55,000 tonne Obo Venture out of Skikda for the U.S. or Northwest Europe for loading February 17. Two to three cargoes each of Skikda and Alexandria, of about 30,000 to 40,000 tonnes, were seen available, as well as some Russian pieces, an Italian trader said.
Gasoline edged up with a rally in futures prices.
High and low sulphur fuel oil failed to follow crude higher. Low sulphur fuel oil was looking less well supplied than last week amid talk that a U.K. utility had bought a cargo.
But offers remain at around $114/$115 cif Italy, with at least two cargoes thought available to load in Northwest Europe in the first half of February.

High sulphur fuel oil was weak again. But ample supplies of Russian barrels loading in the Baltics may push vessels into the Med. At least one E-4 cargo was likely to move from Northwest Europe into the region, traders said. A Suez cargo was heard sold to an Italian refiner at $7 over the high cif of published quotes. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 8167
